To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we show that L6 skeletal muscle and NPU cells are sensitive in vitro models that can be used for assessment of long term toxicity of NPs; (ii) we show that TiO2 and PAA coated magnetic NPs can induce oxidative damage in L6 cells; (iii) we show that internalized TiO2 and magnetic PAA NPs can hinder differentiation of L6 muscle cells
we propose the use of in vitro differentiated cell models as a novel approach to assess long term toxicity of NPs.
L6 cells and NPU are sensitive and robust in vitro models to study short-term and long-term toxic effects of NPs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach to assess the long term toxicity of NPs using two physiologically relevant in vitro models that can differentiate.
the development of a new in vitro model for long term toxicity studies of NPs.
the long term effects of NPs on in vitro models that differentiate, and the potential of these models as a novel approach to predict the long term toxicity of NPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NPU cells are less sensitive than L6 cells to NP exposure.
the L6 cells are a good model to study the long-term effects of NPs, while the NPU cells are not.
the long term toxicity of NPs in vitro is highly dependent on the physico-chemical properties and cell type used for the in vitro exposure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NPs can be taken up by L6 cells and induce oxidative stress.
the L6 cells were more sensitive to NPs than the NPU cells and the NPs were taken up in the L6 cells but were not taken up in the NPU cells.
NPs can cause toxicity in cells that can differentiate and that NPs can hinder differentiation in these cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the in vitro toxicity of NPs depends on the type of NP, the cell type and the exposure protocol.
NPs are not inert and can cause long term effects on cells, even at concentrations that are considered non-toxic in the short term.
NPs can induce oxidative damage in cells and hinder cell differentiation.
